claim: Foot Locker Korea (풋락커코리아 유한회사) FY2025 audit filed on DART 2026-08-12 (Samjong KPMG, report dated 2026-07-31): all 13 Korean stores closed by 2025-06-30 (last = Hongdae), accounts prepared on a liquidation basis, liquidation planned for 2026 but no board resolution yet; net loss KRW 23.18bn (2024) and KRW 17.10bn (2025); 100% owned by Foot Locker Asia Pte. Ltd. (Singapore).
data_point: 2025 revenue KRW 16,230,474,495 (2024: 50,571,685,788); gross profit 462m (2024: 17.17bn); operating loss (9,214,955,329) (2024: (14,050,689,708)); non-operating expenses 8,146,298,875 (2024: 10,618,493,171 incl. tangible-asset impairment 6,459,937,789); net loss (17,103,239,066) (2024: (23,181,312,803)). Payable to Foot Locker Asia Pte. Ltd. KRW 14,368,194 thousand at YE25. [d] 2024+2025 net loss KRW 40.3bn, about $29M at about 1,400 KRW/USD, about $2.2M per store (13 stores); includes run-off operating losses, so the per-store exit cost is an upper-bound inference.
source_name: DART audit report 풋락커코리아 FY2025 (Samjong KPMG)
original_quote: 당사는 청산을 계획하고 있으나, 청산에 대한 이사회 결의는 없었습니다. 다만, 청산계획에 따라 2025년 6월 30일에 홍대점 폐업을 등록하면서 총 13개였던 모든 매장이폐업 되었습니다.
english_translation: The Company plans to liquidate, but there has been no board resolution on liquidation. However, in line with the liquidation plan, with the Hongdae store's closure registered on 30 June 2025, all 13 stores have closed.
verifier_note: Verified directly on DART viewer (dcmNo 11520040): auditor emphasis of matter ('2025년도 6월까지 모든 매장은 폐업... 법인 청산을 2026년도에 예정... 청산기준으로 작성'), income statement figures and parent/payable match exactly. Baseline already has the Korea exit, the Q1 FY25 store table (FL Asia 11 -> 0 by 5/3/25) and a $9M lease-termination benefit in Q2 FY25; the loss size, liquidation-basis accounts and unresolved liquidation are new. Minor timing difference: FL 8-K shows all Korean stores closed by 5/3/25 while DART has the last closure registration on 6/30/25 (registration vs trading). The 2023 net loss of KRW 1.48bn comes from the FY24 audit and was not re-verified; the scraper's 'KRW 40bn wind-down cost' is total 2024-25 net loss, not incremental, so treat per-store cost as inference.

claim: Metro Brands, FL's India licensee, has deliberately slowed Foot Locker store openings because BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) quality-control orders restrict imported product; management repeated this on the Oct-2025, Jan-2026, May-2026 and Aug-2026 calls.
data_point: Q2 FY26 (call Oct-2025): only 4 FL stores opened in the quarter because of BIS. Q3 FY26 (2026-01-28): analyst cites '6 stores'; CFO Kaushal Parekh: 'we will not be aggressively scouting for space for Foot Locker'. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-21): CEO Nissan Joseph: aspiration was 'a lot more stores'. Q1 FY27 (Aug-2026) summary: FL and MetroActiv 'being tested carefully because of operational and regulatory friction'.
source_name: Metro Brands earnings call transcripts Q2 FY26 to Q1 FY27 (AlphaSpread)
original_quote: I think the aspiration was to open a lot more stores by now if we had the comfort of BIS. We still don't have it.
verifier_note: All four AlphaSpread transcript pages fetched (HTTP 200); quotes found verbatim: Q2 FY26 'only open 4 stores this quarter... had we not had BIS', Q3 FY26 '6 stores' (said by analyst Akhil Parekh, not management) and Parekh's 'not be aggressively scouting', Q4 FY26 Joseph quote, Q1 FY27 'tested carefully' (from the AlphaSpread AI summary, not verbatim management speech). The 'imported high-heat = about 20% of FL sales' figure was not located and is unverified. Baseline only lists India/Metro as a licensing partner.
